1. Discotrade skips mid-mission rulings 🔗 Cross-repo conflict ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>The new decisions-kit route tells operators to apply an owner file and use go, relying on the
>added §R instruction to make the builder carry out its steps. Discotrade’s active mission 20 brief
>has an older §R without that instruction, so a mid-mission decisions kit can be committed while the
>resumed builder continues from its checkpoint without acting on the ruling.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[templates/BUILDER-N-PROMPT.md[R98-101]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/6/files#diff-4abca313f3571f857a4d82f471a44d49fcb38a568dba8775b9e3aa7e82e30dcaR98-R101) > >```diff >+the answer came with a file to commit first. If a `plan: decisions >+(owner)` commit is on the branch after the checkpoint's last update and the >+checkpoint does not record its "For the builder" steps as done, carry them >+out first, record them in the checkpoint, and continue. >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Hands makes the new route depend on §R, but discotrade’s current §R only describes dirty-tree
>recovery; its checkpoint shows that mission is still in progress.
>
> > [hands -> discotrade](https://app.qodo.ai/management/relationships?repoId=77e6b9e3-9009-4fbe-bd8c-e1c4bd92a98f&relatedRepoId=f8bc154f-fef0-4515-a253-775ba818fa12&view=table) > [templates/BUILDER-N-PROMPT.md\[95-101\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/ce2088b445d74fe90974f0e358795dba50843432/templates/BUILDER-N-PROMPT.md/#L95-L101) > [docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md\[843-853\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/ce2088b445d74fe90974f0e358795dba50843432/docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md/#L843-L853) > [External repo: SigorMatt/discotrade, meta/BUILDER-20-PROMPT.md \[128-136\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/discotrade/blob/4ed47b479a493492b5c6ba805bffd8271b76a8fd/meta/BUILDER-20-PROMPT.md/#L128-L136) > [External repo: SigorMatt/discotrade, meta/CHECKPOINT.md \[3-9\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/discotrade/blob/4ed47b479a493492b5c6ba805bffd8271b76a8fd/meta/CHECKPOINT.md/#L3-L9) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The decisions-kit-and-go route depends on recovery wording absent from discotrade’s active brief. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- templates/BUILDER-N-PROMPT.md[98-101] >- docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md[843-853] >- meta/BUILDER-20-PROMPT.md[128-136] > >## Recommended Fix >Update discotrade’s active and future mission briefs with the owner-file recovery rule before recommending this route there, or provide a compatible route for briefs that lack it. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

2. Failed consults leave the pipeline running 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability
>
>Description >
> >
>_consult_for_human persists an unpause before it calls enqueue, without restoring the stop if
>enqueue fails. A queue or spool failure can therefore leave a stopped pipeline running even though
>no architect consultation was created.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/playbook.py[R2542-2545]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/6/files#diff-d4c45908377a317f0fbbccad6f8af7a74c4af564c4272d3cecc7126bf1be9204R2542-R2545) > >```diff >+ self._unpause("resume") >+ started = await self.enqueue( >+ role=ARCHITECT, >+ context="clear", >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The new path saves the resumed state before awaiting enqueue; daemon enqueue can reject queue
>admission or fail while creating the job, and the API catches only consultation-specific refusals.
>
> > [src/hands/playbook.py\[2533-2551\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/ce2088b445d74fe90974f0e358795dba50843432/src/hands/playbook.py/#L2533-L2551) > [src/hands/daemon.py\[543-580\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/ce2088b445d74fe90974f0e358795dba50843432/src/hands/daemon.py/#L543-L580) > [src/hands/api.py\[600-609\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/ce2088b445d74fe90974f0e358795dba50843432/src/hands/api.py/#L600-L609) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A failed human-consult enqueue currently clears a persisted pipeline stop without starting a consultation. >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/playbook.py[2533-2566] >- src/hands/api.py[593-609] >## Recommended Fix >Make job creation succeed before persisting the unpause, or restore the prior stopped state on enqueue failure. Keep the consultation event consistent with the created job. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

3. Exhausted jobs stay stopped after resume 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>The operator table tells a human to run resume after a limits.max_resumes reached stop, but that
>command only clears the pipeline pause. When the resume limit has been reached, the limit manager
>schedules no new builder job, so following this row does not restart the work.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md[908]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/6/files#diff-2ad26343d21a57c4b0e1450bc61bad64fd9ee975037b345cdcf9841cdab2905eR908-R908) > >```diff >+| `hands: the pipeline stopped` — limits.max_resumes reached: has been resumed time(s) with no `done` in between and is limited again | the human alone — route 7 | after the capture, `resume ` | `bash scripts/capture-quota-stop.sh `, then `hands resume` | >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The limit manager returns without scheduling a resume at the maximum, while the public resume API
>delegates to a pipeline unpause rather than job creation.
>
> > [src/hands/limits.py\[361-399\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/ce2088b445d74fe90974f0e358795dba50843432/src/hands/limits.py/#L361-L399) > [src/hands/api.py\[1524-1533\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/ce2088b445d74fe90974f0e358795dba50843432/src/hands/api.py/#L1524-L1533) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[3072-3092\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/ce2088b445d74fe90974f0e358795dba50843432/src/hands/playbook.py/#L3072-L3092) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The exhausted-resume row prescribes a command that unpauses the pipeline but does not restart its limited job. >## Fix Focus Areas >- docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md[868-874] >- docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md[907-908] >## Recommended Fix >Give `max_resumes reached` its own recovery route that identifies how the human resolves the exhausted limit and starts work again. Reserve the ordinary `resume` instruction for the case where the limit manager has scheduled a job resume. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

4. Ruling follow-ups refuse consultation 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>Route 5 says to send an owner kit using route 4 and then run consult, but route 4 ends by running
>go. If the human follows that sequence immediately, go starts a builder job and the new consult
>path refuses the request while that job is queued or running.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md[R857-859]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/6/files#diff-2ad26343d21a57c4b0e1450bc61bad64fd9ee975037b345cdcf9841cdab2905eR857-R859) > >```diff >+ blocked mission under a playbook without the blocked→consult rule): any >+ owner file first, as route 4's kit; then `consult ` (§16); >+ at the laptop `hands consult`. >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The two new routes prescribe go followed by consult; the phone go path starts builder work, and
>consult_refusal rejects builder jobs in running, queued, or held states.
>
> > [docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md\[840-859\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/ce2088b445d74fe90974f0e358795dba50843432/docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md/#L840-L859) > [src/hands/phone.py\[493-516\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/ce2088b445d74fe90974f0e358795dba50843432/src/hands/phone.py/#L493-L516) > [src/hands/api.py\[584-590\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/ce2088b445d74fe90974f0e358795dba50843432/src/hands/api.py/#L584-L590) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The consultation route inherits a `go` command that makes the ensuing consultation fail its builder-busy check. >## Fix Focus Areas >- docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md[843-859] >- docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md[924-925] >## Recommended Fix >Spell out when the owner kit has finished applying and when, if at all, `go` should run. If `go` is required first, instruct the human to wait for its builder job to end before issuing `consult`. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

5. Rejected consults fill the kit directory 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability
>
>Description >
> >
>_consult_command leaves the permanently linked attachment in kit_dir when UTF-8 decoding or the
>final consultation check refuses it. Repeated authenticated requests with invalid text, or requests
>refused after a state change during download, accumulate files even though no consultation starts.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/phone.py[R624-628]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/6/files#diff-6d175ae5f33f6b544ecf5e01493181c805135928b88647bc51a3ff9971544b75R624-R628) > >```diff >+ data = await asyncio.to_thread((directory / written).read_bytes) >+ attached = consult_file_text(data, "the attachment") >+ except (OSError, ValueError) as exc: >+ problem = str(exc) if isinstance(exc, ValueError) else type(exc).__name__ >+ return await self._refuse("consult", problem) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The download links a permanent named file and cleans only its temporary file; both subsequent
>refusal branches return without deleting the permanent attachment.
>
> > [src/hands/phone.py\[617-632\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/ce2088b445d74fe90974f0e358795dba50843432/src/hands/phone.py/#L617-L632) > [src/hands/phone.py\[1034-1043\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/ce2088b445d74fe90974f0e358795dba50843432/src/hands/phone.py/#L1034-L1043) > [src/hands/api.py\[593-608\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/ce2088b445d74fe90974f0e358795dba50843432/src/hands/api.py/#L593-L608) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A phone consult can retain a downloaded attachment after refusing the command, allowing unused files to accumulate. >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/phone.py[617-632] >- src/hands/phone.py[1034-1043] >## Recommended Fix >Track the path returned by `_fetch` and remove that specific newly written file if decoding or `start_consult` fails. Preserve attachments for successfully started consultations. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

6. A refused consult can stop a running pipeline 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability
>
>Description >
> >
>Api.consult_refusal calls engine.reload(), which runs the full PlaybookEngine._load(), before
>it checks for a busy builder, aux or architect. _load() stops and pauses the pipeline when the
>playbook does not load (dirty, uncommitted, wrong config). It also swaps the in-memory playbook and
>clears last_rule in the middle of a running job. So a phone consult (asked twice, before and
>after the fetch) or a hands consult sent while the builder is working can stop the pipeline. It
>can also change which rules decide that builder's end, even though the consult itself is then
>refused as busy.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/api.py[R569-576]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/6/files#diff-16f021e493ba18b1e5f11a7ee4f78300324921ac8ae5a15bbe45cab098c59139R569-R576) > >```diff >+ engine = self.daemon.playbook >+ await engine.reload() >+ why = engine.consult_mode_refusal() >+ if why is not None: >+ return why >+ why = self._role_busy(ARCHITECT_ROLE) >+ if why is not None: >+ return why >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>consult_refusal awaits engine.reload() first. reload() is await self._load(). On a
>PlaybookError, _load calls self.stop(...), which sets paused=True, appends a stop event
>and notifies 'the pipeline stopped' whenever the pipeline is not already paused. On success it
>replaces self.playbook, re-anchors the series and clears last_rule when the sha changed.
>Elsewhere this only happens when a job starts (on_job_start). The busy-role refusals
>(_role_busy) only run after the reload.
>
> > [src/hands/api.py\[557-591\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/ce2088b445d74fe90974f0e358795dba50843432/src/hands/api.py/#L557-L591) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[1623-1677\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/ce2088b445d74fe90974f0e358795dba50843432/src/hands/playbook.py/#L1623-L1677) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[2990-3032\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/ce2088b445d74fe90974f0e358795dba50843432/src/hands/playbook.py/#L2990-L3032) > [src/hands/phone.py\[613-632\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/ce2088b445d74fe90974f0e358795dba50843432/src/hands/phone.py/#L613-L632) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >`Api.consult_refusal` reloads the playbook through `PlaybookEngine._load()` before it checks for busy roles. `_load()` can call `stop()`, which pauses the pipeline and notifies. It also replaces the playbook in force and clears `last_rule` while a job is running. So a consult that is going to be refused anyway can stop a running pipeline or change the rules for the running job. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/api.py[557-591] >- src/hands/playbook.py[1623-1627] > >## Recommended Fix >Run the `_role_busy` checks for architect/builder/aux, and the `kit_wait` check, before calling `engine.reload()`. Only reload once no role is busy. Also make `reload()` side-effect free on failure: load the playbook without `stop()` (for example, a `_load(stop_on_error=False)` variant that only sets `load_error`), so the refusal text reports the load error without stopping the pipeline. Add a test: a consult sent while a builder job is running with a dirty playbook leaves `pipeline.json` unpaused and `last_rule` unchanged. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/6a5a3002-45ce-4425-843b-6e2595874939?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/6a5a3002-45ce-4425-843b-6e2595874939)
7. Discotrade consultations lack reviews 🔗 Cross-repo conflict ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>human_consult_prompt replaces the review with a reason and starts the architect with no review
>job. Discotrade’s standing architect instructions require a consultation on a review outcome and
>require reading the review it names, leaving that required input undefined when its operator uses
>the new consult command.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/playbook.py[R3406-3410]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/6/files#diff-d4c45908377a317f0fbbccad6f8af7a74c4af564c4272d3cecc7126bf1be9204R3406-R3410) > >```diff >+def human_consult_prompt(reason: str, brief: ArchitectBrief | None = None) -> str: >+ """§42: the architect consult prompt of a consultation the human started — §31's >+ prompt with the review's sections replaced by the human's reason, verbatim, under >+ `HUMAN_REASON_HEADING`; its first line is `HUMAN_HEAD`.""" >+ return _architect_prompt(HUMAN_EVENT, None, brief, reason=reason) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The new prompt explicitly supplies a human reason instead of a review, while discotrade’s
>project-specific instructions mandate a review outcome and a named review.
>
> > [hands -> discotrade](https://app.qodo.ai/management/relationships?repoId=77e6b9e3-9009-4fbe-bd8c-e1c4bd92a98f&relatedRepoId=f8bc154f-fef0-4515-a253-775ba818fa12&view=table) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[3406-3415\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/ce2088b445d74fe90974f0e358795dba50843432/src/hands/playbook.py/#L3406-L3415) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[3352-3365\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/ce2088b445d74fe90974f0e358795dba50843432/src/hands/playbook.py/#L3352-L3365) > [External repo: SigorMatt/discotrade, meta/ARCHITECT.md \[1-5\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/discotrade/blob/4ed47b479a493492b5c6ba805bffd8271b76a8fd/meta/ARCHITECT.md/#L1-L5) > [External repo: SigorMatt/discotrade, meta/ARCHITECT.md \[30-43\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/discotrade/blob/4ed47b479a493492b5c6ba805bffd8271b76a8fd/meta/ARCHITECT.md/#L30-L43) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Human-started consultations omit the review required by discotrade’s standing architect procedure. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/playbook.py[3406-3410] >- meta/ARCHITECT.md[1-5] >- meta/ARCHITECT.md[30-43] > >## Recommended Fix >Update discotrade’s architect instructions to define the human-reason path, including what replaces the named review when deciding whether to file a kit or escalate, before enabling that command for the project. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
